text:
Elaine (sales): Ashley from FinPlat just pinged — they need an EU-only attestation + subprocessor inventory for a 2-week POC. can we turn this around today?

Ashley (customer): Hi all. POC will run in eu-west1 + eu-central1. Requirement: 1) explicit statement that, under the requested config, no request or log leaves EU; 2) subprocessor list for any service that can observe payloads; 3) exactly what triggers a failover and whether it's manual/automatic + telemetry we can use. Legal needs this for POC signoff.

James (solutions): quick Q: do you require BYOK for POC or is managed keys ok? impacts KMS call locations.

Ashley (customer): managed keys fine for POC. BYOK is optional later.

Miguel (eng-infra): technically we can enforce tenant pinning to EU + disable automatic cross-region failover. that keeps traffic on EU-hosted infra. components touching traffic (short):
- redwood-edge-proxy (eu-west1, eu-central1)
- regional-inference-pool (gpu nodes in eu regions)
- metrics aggregator (prometheus replica in eu)
- logging pipeline (customer logs stay in eu unless customer config forwards elsewhere)
- optional 3rd-party monitoring (not enabled by default)

Tara (security): i'll prepare a 1-paragraph attestation and include links to our subprocessors page. Miguel please flag any subprocessors that have access to payload-level logs.

Miguel (eng-infra): logging pipeline sends structured logs to a customer-configured sink. default retention and storage are in eu. if customer enables external SIEM forwarding, that would leave EU — but we won't enable that for the POC.

Olivia (legal): we need subprocessors + geo of data centers for legal. also a brief statement on audit trails and approval flow for any manual failover.

James (solutions): adding the API/console snippet for tenant routing toggle (to include in the runbook):
```
PATCH /v1/tenants/<tenant_id>/routing
{
  "tenant_pin": true,
  "allow_cross_region_failover": false
}
```
Console path: Console -> Tenants -> <tenant> -> Routing -> Enable "Pin to Region" + Disable "Cross-region failover"

Ashley (customer): perfect. also need a cost note: if we pin capacity to eu, any rough percent delta on committed usage?

Miguel (eng-infra): rough estimate: pinning increases reserved capacity skew — expect ~6-10% uplift on committed GPU utilization for small POCs due to less flexible pooling. i'll give a short table in the artifact.

Tara (security): attestation draft: "Redwood Inference attests that when tenant_pin is enabled and allow_cross_region_failover is disabled, customer request ingress, LLM processing, and default logging/storage are handled exclusively by EU-hosted infrastructure and subprocessors. Any cross-border data transfer is only performed following an explicit, documented customer approval process. Optional third-party SaaS agents are disabled by default for this POC." will append signatures and a pointer to our subprocessors registry.

Ashley (customer): that wording is good. can you also show an observable metric we can monitor to ensure nothing failed over?

Miguel (eng-infra): recommend monitoring these during POC:
- routing.route_region (tagged metric) -> should be eu-west1 or eu-central1
- infra.failover_events.count -> should be 0
- egress.bytes_by_region -> should report EU only
- logs.forwarding.destination -> check it's blank / set to EU sink
I can add Grafana URLs and alert rules in the runbook.

DeployBot: reminder: attach the CSV subprocessor export as a secure link, do not paste credentials.

Elaine (sales): plan: Miguel export CSV with columns (service,name,region,subprocessor,can_see_payload,default_enabled), Tara finalizes attestation, James writes runbook snippet + UI/API steps, Olivia confirms legal language. i'll send combined package to Ashley + legal by 17:00 UTC.

Ashley (customer): thanks all. one more tiny ask — can you mark any subprocessor that may have config-only visibility vs payload visibility?

Miguel (eng-infra): will flag as CAN_VIEW_PAYLOAD or CONFIG_ONLY in CSV. note on optional SaaS: marked as CONFIG_ONLY and NOT ENABLED_FOR_POC.

Tara (security): adding small appendix on audit: all tenant routing changes are recorded in audit logs with actor, timestamp, and before/after state. manual failover requires an ops ticket and customer approval by default.

Elaine (sales): great. ping me when artifacts are ready. @Miguel @Tara @James @Olivia please react with :white_check_mark: when done.

Miguel (eng-infra): working on CSV now.

Tara (security): attestation ready, will attach secure link in thread when file uploaded.

James (solutions): runbook snippet + console screenshots uploaded.

Olivia (legal): reviewed language and ok to include in POC signoff package.

DeployBot: uploaded links detected: subproc-inventory.csv (secure), attestation.pdf (secure), runbook.md (secure).

Elaine (sales): sending package to Ashley and legal now. thanks team! :partyparrot:

Ashley (customer): received the package, thanks. will loop in compliance for final signoff. :thumbsup:
